title: Design a Zero-Stall Raft Log Compaction & Snapshot Streaming Engine

spark.summary: Design a Raft log compaction and snapshot streaming subsystem for a 50K writes/sec consensus cluster that bounds WAL size under 1 GB, sustains sub-10ms write P99, and recovers restarted followers in < 45 seconds.
spark.keyTakeaway: Combine RocksDB hard-link checkpoints, jittered dual compaction triggers, priority heartbeat lanes, and token-bucket InstallSnapshot streaming.
spark.byteSummary:
In a 50,000 writes/sec consensus cluster (such as etcd or Kafka KRaft), naive log compaction introduces two failure modes: stop-the-world state-machine freezes during snapshot serialization, and NIC saturation during unthrottled `InstallSnapshot` transfers that starve heartbeats and trigger split-brain election storms.

The target engine triggers compaction via jittered dual thresholds (`100K entries OR 256 MB WAL`), forks an O(1) RocksDB hard-link checkpoint (or CoW clone) in < 1 ms without pausing the Raft apply loop, fsyncs CRC32C-verified snapshot chunks, and retains a 10K-entry WAL suffix.

When a follower restarts behind `firstLogIndex`, the leader streams `InstallSnapshot` chunks through a token-bucket rate limiter (capping snapshot traffic at 50% NIC bandwidth) while routing `AppendEntries` heartbeats on a separate priority lane with PreVote enabled—delivering sub-10ms write P99 and < 45s follower recovery.

learningJourney.title: Stage 1: SLO Framing — Bounded WAL, Sub-10ms P99 & < 45s Recovery
learningJourney.purpose: Define disk bounds, write-latency targets, and recovery-time objectives for a 50K writes/sec Raft group.
learningJourney.explanation: At 50K writes/sec (~40 MB/s WAL append rate), the compaction engine must keep uncompacted WAL under 256-512 MB per node, avoid any write-path P99 spike > 10 ms during snapshotting, and recover a wiped/restarted follower (e.g., 4 GB compressed snapshot) in < 45 seconds without disturbing leader stability.

sectionDiagram.title: Balancing Disk Bounds, Write P99 & Follower Recovery Speed

cards.label: 32-Second Transfer
cards.detail: A 4 GB compressed snapshot streams at 1 Gbps (125 MB/s) in ~32 seconds, leaving 13 seconds for suffix replay.

cards.label: Zero Quorum Disruption
cards.detail: Maintaining < 10 ms P99 ensures Raft client leases and ReadIndex queries never time out.

sectionDiagram.summary: The engine targets <= 256 MB uncompacted WAL, < 10 ms write P99 during compaction, and < 45s follower recovery.
sectionDiagram.caption: 50K writes/sec consensus engine targets <= 256 MB WAL, < 10 ms write P99, and < 45s follower recovery.

learningJourney.title: Stage 2: Compaction State Machine & Jittered Dual Triggers
learningJourney.purpose: Design non-overlapping compaction triggers so replicas never compact simultaneously.
learningJourney.explanation: Each Raft node evaluates `uncompacted_entries >= entry_thresh OR wal_bytes >= byte_thresh` after committing an apply batch. Adding +/-15% node-specific jitter (seeded by `node_id`) prevents all 3-5 replicas from entering compaction at the exact same index and spiking cluster-wide tail latency.

sectionDiagram.title: Jittered Dual-Threshold Compaction Controller

cards.label: Single-Flight Guard
cards.detail: If a previous snapshot is still streaming to disk, skip triggering a second concurrent compaction.

cards.label: Staggered Replicas
cards.detail: Jitter ensures at least a majority of replicas remain unburdened by compaction I/O at any instant.

sectionDiagram.summary: Jittered dual thresholds and a single-flight compaction guard stagger replica snapshots and prevent overlapping builds.
sectionDiagram.caption: Apply batch monitor applies +/-15% node jitter and single-flight gating before launching background compaction.

learningJourney.title: Stage 3: Zero-Stall Checkpoint Fork & Streaming Checksums
learningJourney.purpose: Implement O(1) RocksDB hard-link checkpoints with Zstd compression and per-chunk CRC32C.
learningJourney.explanation: On trigger, the apply thread invokes `rocksdb::Checkpoint::CreateCheckpoint()` (creating hard-links to immutable SSTables and copying the small active memtable) in < 1 ms, tagging `(lastIncludedIndex, lastIncludedTerm)`. A background thread tars/Zstd-compresses the checkpoint into 4 MB chunks with CRC32C trailers and atomically commits `snapshot.meta`.

sectionDiagram.title: O(1) RocksDB Checkpoint -> Zstd + CRC32C Background Pipeline

cards.label: Zstd Level 3 Sweet Spot
cards.detail: Zstd level 3 compresses KV snapshots ~2.5x at 400+ MB/s per core, cutting network transfer time in half.

cards.label: Bounded I/O Nice
cards.detail: Run background compression with cgroup/ionice throttling so foreground WAL fsyncs keep < 2 ms latency.

sectionDiagram.summary: RocksDB hard-link checkpoints plus background Zstd-3 compression and CRC32C framing build durable snapshots without blocking writes.
sectionDiagram.caption: RocksDB CreateCheckpoint() hands immutable SSTables to a background Zstd + CRC32C pipeline.

learningJourney.title: Stage 4: WAL Segment Rotation & Suffix-Preserving GC
learningJourney.purpose: Reclaim disk space safely via fixed-size WAL segments while keeping a 10K-entry suffix.
learningJourney.explanation: Store the Raft WAL as 64 MB sealed segments (`wal-000001.log`, `wal-000002.log`). After a snapshot is durably committed at `S`, the WAL garbage collector unlinks any sealed segment whose `max_index <= S - 10,000`, reclaiming disk in O(1) `unlink()` calls without rewriting active log files.

sectionDiagram.title: O(1) Unlink of Sealed 64 MB WAL Segments Behind Suffix Cutoff

cards.label: Zero In-Place Rewrite
cards.detail: Segmented WALs avoid copying remaining suffix entries during truncation—just unlink old segment files.

cards.label: Active-Cursor Pinning
cards.detail: Ref-counting sealed segments prevents deleting a file while an AppendEntries batch is still reading it.

sectionDiagram.summary: 64 MB segmented WALs let the GC unlink obsolete prefixes in O(1) while preserving a 10K-entry suffix for minor follower lag.
sectionDiagram.caption: Segmented 64 MB WAL files are unlinked in O(1) once their max_index falls behind snapIdx - 10,000.

learningJourney.title: Stage 5: Token-Bucket InstallSnapshot & Priority Heartbeat Lane
learningJourney.purpose: Stream snapshots to lagging followers without starving AppendEntries heartbeats or saturating NICs.
learningJourney.explanation: Leaders maintain two gRPC/TCP channels per peer: a high-priority control channel for `AppendEntries` heartbeats and `RequestVote`, and a bulk data channel for `InstallSnapshot` chunks. A token-bucket limiter caps snapshot egress at 50% NIC capacity (and max 2 concurrent peers) so heartbeats always arrive in < 10 ms.

sectionDiagram.title: Dual-Channel Raft Transport: Priority Heartbeats vs. Paced Snapshots

cards.label: No Head-of-Line Blocking
cards.detail: Separate TCP connections prevent a 4 MB snapshot chunk from delaying a 64-byte heartbeat packet.

cards.label: Staggered Multi-Node Rebuild
cards.detail: Capping concurrent snapshot streams at 2 prevents 3 simultaneous node restarts from saturating leader egress.

sectionDiagram.summary: Separating heartbeats onto a priority lane and pacing InstallSnapshot chunks via token buckets keeps quorum stable during rebuilds.
sectionDiagram.caption: Priority heartbeat connections and token-bucket-paced bulk channels isolate quorum liveness from snapshot transfers.

learningJourney.title: Stage 6: Resumable Snapshot Transfers & PreVote Election Safety
learningJourney.purpose: Handle mid-transfer network drops and prevent partitioned followers from disrupting the leader.
learningJourney.explanation: If a follower loses connectivity at byte offset 2.5 GB of a 4 GB snapshot, resumable chunking (keyed by `snapshot_id` + `offset`) lets the follower continue from 2.5 GB instead of restarting from 0. Meanwhile, `PreVote` ensures any lagging or briefly congested follower checks whether a majority would vote for it before incrementing `currentTerm`.

sectionDiagram.title: Offset-Resumable Transfers & PreVote Term Protection

cards.label: Snapshot Pinning
cards.detail: The leader pins the active snapshot_id in memory/disk until transfer completes or times out so GC won't delete it mid-stream.

cards.label: Zero Spurious Term Bumps
cards.detail: PreVote stops isolated followers from forcing healthy leaders to step down upon reconnection.

sectionDiagram.summary: Keying chunks by snapshot_id enables offset resumption after drops, while PreVote shields the leader from spurious term bumps.
sectionDiagram.caption: Resumable snapshot_id offsets avoid full restarts on network drops, and PreVote blocks spurious leader elections.

learningJourney.title: Stage 7: Operational Telemetry, Corruption Drills & ReadIndex
learningJourney.purpose: Monitor compaction lag, verify snapshot checksums in CI/chaos drills, and uphold ReadIndex linearizability.
learningJourney.explanation: Track `raft_wal_bytes`, `raft_snapshot_duration_ms`, and `raft_install_snapshot_active_peers` with alerts if WAL exceeds 2x threshold. Run automated chaos drills that corrupt a chunk's CRC32C (verifying clean rejection) and validate that `ReadIndex` queries remain linearizable across follower snapshot swaps.

sectionDiagram.title: WAL Lag Telemetry, CRC Chaos Drills & ReadIndex Verification

cards.label: Snapshot-Before-GC Alert
cards.detail: If disk usage rises while snapshots fail, alert immediately before the node hits ENOSPC.

cards.label: Linearizability Invariant
cards.detail: A follower that just installed a snapshot at index S never serves ReadIndex < S.

sectionDiagram.summary: WAL-size alerts, CRC32C fault-injection drills, and ReadIndex checks keep the compaction engine production-safe.
sectionDiagram.caption: Prometheus WAL alerts, CRC32C fault drills, and ReadIndex monotonicity checks verify production safety.

knowledgeChecks.question: Why does a Raft leader separate `AppendEntries` heartbeats onto a priority connection distinct from `InstallSnapshot`?

options.text: To prevent 4 MB snapshot chunks from causing head-of-line blocking and delaying heartbeats past `electionTimeout`.
options.feedback: Correct. Separate priority connections ensure heartbeats stay under 10 ms even during multi-gigabyte transfers.

options.text: Because TCP does not support files larger than 1 MB.
options.feedback: Incorrect. TCP streams arbitrary bytes, but large chunks cause head-of-line queueing delays.

options.text: Because `AppendEntries` uses UDP while `InstallSnapshot` uses HTTP/1.1.
options.feedback: Incorrect. Both typically run over TCP/gRPC.

options.text: To bypass CRC32C checksum verification on heartbeats.
options.feedback: Incorrect. Separate lanes are for QoS and head-of-line isolation.

knowledgeChecks.explanation: Isolating heartbeats on a dedicated priority lane prevents large snapshot chunks from delaying heartbeats and triggering election storms.

knowledgeChecks.question: What is the purpose of adding +/-15% node-ID jitter to Raft compaction thresholds?

options.text: To stagger snapshots across replicas so the entire quorum never incurs compaction I/O simultaneously.
options.feedback: Correct. Jittering thresholds keeps a majority of replicas fast and unburdened at any point in time.

options.text: To randomize `lastIncludedTerm` so leaders change faster.
options.feedback: Incorrect. lastIncludedTerm is a deterministic log term, never randomized.
Incorrect. Every node must still fsync snapshots before truncating WALs.
Incorrect. InstallSnapshot is always required when the needed prefix has been compacted.

knowledgeChecks.explanation: Per-node threshold jitter prevents synchronized compaction pauses across all replicas in a Raft group.

knowledgeChecks.question: If a follower crashes while receiving chunk 50 of 100 in `InstallSnapshot`, why is its existing state machine still intact on restart?

options.text: Because chunks are staged in `snapshot.tmp` and the state machine is only swapped atomically after `done == true` and CRC32C verification.
options.feedback: Correct. Staging in a temp file and atomically renaming on completion ensures partial transfers never corrupt live state.

options.text: Because Raft followers never write snapshots to disk.
options.feedback: Incorrect. Followers must durably persist snapshots before acknowledging and truncating.

options.text: Because `PreVote` rolls back the leader's snapshot.
options.feedback: Incorrect. PreVote only governs leader elections.

options.text: Because the leader deletes its own snapshot after chunk 50.
options.feedback: Incorrect. Leaders pin the snapshot until transfer completes.

knowledgeChecks.explanation: Staging incoming chunks in a temporary file and atomically swapping only after done=true and checksum validation makes snapshot installation crash-safe.

beginner.summary: Build a Raft snapshot system that takes fast background checkpoints, deletes old log files safely, and streams snapshots to restarting nodes in under 45 seconds.
beginner.keyTakeaway: Background checkpoints and rate-limited snapshot streaming keep the cluster fast while recovering failed nodes.
beginner.byteSummary: To keep a Raft database fast at 50,000 writes/sec, nodes take quick background snapshots, delete older log files once the snapshot is safe on disk, and stream snapshots in paced chunks to restarting followers.

intermediate.summary: Use O(1) RocksDB checkpoints, 64 MB segmented WAL GC with a 10K-entry suffix, and dual-lane `InstallSnapshot` + priority heartbeats.
intermediate.keyTakeaway: Jittered dual triggers (100K entries or 256 MB WAL) and token-bucket snapshot pacing maintain < 10 ms write P99 and < 45s recovery.
intermediate.byteSummary: The engine uses `RocksDB CreateCheckpoint()` (< 1 ms) and Zstd-3 + CRC32C background framing, unlinks sealed 64 MB WAL segments behind `snapIdx - 10,000`, and paces `InstallSnapshot` at 50% NIC capacity on a separate bulk lane.

advanced.summary: Add `snapshot_id` offset-resumable transfers, `PreVote` term protection, cgroup/ionice background throttling, and CRC32C chaos drills.
advanced.keyTakeaway: Resumable offset transfers avoid restarting multi-GB rebuilds on transient drops, while `PreVote` and priority heartbeats eliminate election storms.
advanced.byteSummary: Production hardening pairs `snapshot_id`-pinned offset resumption (avoiding 0-byte restarts on link drops) with `PreVote` election guards, `ionice` background compression, 2x WAL-threshold alerting, and automated CRC32C fault-injection drills.
